## Survey open-0: LIN-4475 @ b937237a4

Heads read: LinearViewer `b937237a4`; simple-dispatcher `47fb6af`, which is later than the ticket's grounding `1616b19c3` because PR 1 (LIN-4474, #340) has since merged. SD facts below come from `47fb6af`.

**1. Filling the `sd` cells clashes with PR 1's new rule.** The ticket copies this PR's head `contract.json` into an unmerged SD branch and names that SD commit in LV's header. LIN-4474's header in SD `test/runner-contract.test.js:27-30` says to copy "only from a merged LinearViewer `main` commit … never from a PR head or an unmerged branch". The named SD commit also gets rebased away, so each repo pins the other's pre-merge commit. Way through: call the prepared branch verification only, in LV's header and PR description. SD PR 3 then re-copies from merged LV main and re-pins `LV_COMMIT`/`FIXTURE_SHA256` (`:52-54`). Say so on LIN-4461.

**2. The census doesn't match the rows.** "Every session value in use has an unhalted follow-up row" fails for `none`. Both `none` rows are halted, and the ticket adds unhalted rows only for `finished`, `running` and `stopped`. The census must also say whether the unhalted `repo` row "unknown repo on a follow-up" counts. SD fails no-session follow-ups (`followup.js` `no-session`), so an unhalted `none` row is cheap.

**3. The unknown-repo fixture has to say `running`.** `setup()` writes a ledger whose only row is `running`, and the ticket keeps it. "A follow-up carrying an unknown repo is continued" passes only if its id is in that ledger. With `finished` and no `done` row, `resolveFollowUp` rejects it. So the fixture diverges from its renamed contract row.

**4. The fold change can't be seen in the corpus.** The kit drops synthetic records after folding, keyed on the last non-empty model (`runner.mjs` `foldTranscriptMessages`/`transcriptRequestRecords`). SD skips synthetic lines before keying and takes the first usage line's model, keeping `""` (`request-usage.js:60,70`). The 8 corpus stages are byte-identical in both repos but have no split model, missing model or ID-less line, so only the inline cases witness the change. The `lin-4202` `:126` assertion still passes unchanged. Inferred: first-line-even-if-none can produce model-less records that don't price.

**5. Smaller.** Both new report rows already read as the ticket says, in Harbour and in SD (`LINE_BREAK_RE` splits on U+2028, `links.js:257`); I checked by running them. The W6 witness's deliberate failure goes in `gateFacts` in `lib/run-paragraph.js`, not the hook. Lessons are 6,020 of 6,144 bytes. SD's `sdPin` throws on the new `fold` area (`:233`) until `pinFold` exists.

**First:** on a scratch SD branch, write the four-value mapping in `stateFor`/`polledItem` (`:115-131`) and `pinFold`, so the `sd` cells are known before any LV row is written. `live` means COMPLETED there, so the renames are safe.

**Possibly deeper:** the kit claims follow-ups to running or stopped sessions (`resolveFollowUp` continues any row that isn't `lost`). SD refuses both; a second resume would collide on the transcript write. The ticket records this as a `difference`. Whether the kit should refuse too is the real question; this piece only pins the gap.

## Survey global: LIN-4475 @ b937237a4

**Where it lands.** Mostly test and fixture: `contract.json` (66 rows, 12 areas), `tests/unit/runner-kit-contract.test.js` (617 lines), and the kit fold at `lib/runner-kit/runner.mjs:572–651`. Each row's shape is checked well (`AREA_SHAPES` :284, `checkRowShape` :311). The table as a whole is checked only by hand-written counts (:340–361), and the SHA pin (:48) catches byte changes, not meaning. Direction: improving. Each contract step added a census (LIN-3451 → 4384). Lessons are 6,020 of 6,144 bytes, so "no Lesson" is forced.

**Done the obvious way.** It lands cleanly on code being tested, not changed; the risk is a third copy of three things:
- **Session words held only in the test.** The kit names no ledger states: `running/done/stopped/lost` are bare strings at 17 sites (e.g. `runner.mjs:179,446`). `live` already means two things: `resolveFollowUp` (:201) continues anything not `lost`, `done` included, while `recoverAction`'s `out.live` (:440) means running or stopped. `lost` is in neither mapping. A census over values "in use" can't see a value with no rows.
- **A third pin on the eight corpus files**, beside `LIN4197_CASES` (`tests/fixtures/cost-replay/corpus.js:214`) and `lin-4202…test.js:58,74`. `caseKeyOf` is local there, so it gets copied. A scratch copy of the new fold rule, run outside the repo, gave unchanged records on all 8 files: no spread into cost-replay tests, but the corpus doesn't exercise the new rules either.
- **Fold leftovers.** `foldTranscriptMessages` has one caller (:632). `found` is unread (`records.found` at :1273 is a different count), and `keyOf` exists only to count `noId`.
- **Fixture split.** `ledger` (:57) reaches the kit through `ctxFor` (:72), `haltSweep` (:241) and `setup()` (:455, 3 take-driven blocks). A `SESSION_LEDGER` map that throws on `live`, plus `ledgerFor(session)` passed to `ctxFor`, keeps `itemFor` single (one line at :67).
- **Silent drift:** "Waiting N" references at `lib/dispatch-store.js:3546` and `tests/unit/lin-4455-kinds-and-constants-characterization.test.js:18,22` shift again when entries are removed. The guard checks paths, not positions. SD's literal "No live session" (`runner.mjs:205`) must stay.

**Better, at a cost this task can carry:**
- Fold tidy-up: drop `found` and `keyOf`, one skip path (~10–15 lines, guarded by lin-4202).
- One session map that both the driver and the census read, as `HALT_MODES` does (`lib/workspace-halt.js:34`) (~5 lines).
- Export `caseKeyOf` from a shared fixture (~5 lines).
- Fix the stale test header at `runner-kit-contract.test.js:6–11` (~3 lines).
- The `paragraphFacts` comment at `lib/run-paragraph.js:42` is stale (`gateFacts`, :174, is what's hashed). It's production code the task leaves alone, so it belongs in a Waiting entry, not the diff.

**Better still, not this task's:** a whole-table check derived from `AREA_SHAPES` (both repos, with PR 1's work); named kit ledger states with `out.live` renamed (17 sites); a kit refusal for follow-ups to running sessions (`take` continues into one today, :1158; the task declines it).

**Symptom?** Partly. Copies across repos are by design (`runner.mjs:23–24`, a self-contained kit). The double `live` is a symptom of the kit having no named ledger states (inferred), and fixing it in the contract alone leaves `out.live` and `lost` as they were.

No repository content changed.

## Review — LIN-4475

PR https://github.com/JKershaw/LinearViewer/pull/2448, reviewed at head `68b3e5f428740954ffa38d264bcddceb07d6f035` (OPEN, CLEAN). Base is LV `origin/main` `ca77a891e`, which is the merge-base, so main hasn't moved since. SD `origin/main` is still `47fb6af`. I re-checked all three before posting.

CI: green. Run https://github.com/JKershaw/LinearViewer/actions/runs/43531464500 ran on `68b3e5f4`; the check-runs API confirms every check's `head_sha` is that commit. All passed: Unit tests; Unit tests (proxy, clock +400d); E2E shards 1/4, 2/4, 3/4 and 4/4; Secret scan (source); CI success.

**Scope.** Six files changed, and the ask or plan names each one: `lib/runner-kit/contract.json`, `lib/runner-kit/runner.mjs`, `tests/unit/runner-kit-contract.test.js`, `tests/unit/lin-4202-runner-kit-records.test.js`, `tests/unit/run-paragraph-hook.test.js` and `docs/areas/runs-and-dispatch.md`. Nothing goes beyond the plan. The commits on main since the ticket was created touch none of the contract, the kit, the contract test or the fixtures, so nothing is stale. The ask names `tests/fixtures/cost-replay/` as the corpus path; the PR uses the plan's path, `tests/fixtures/runner-kit/transcript-corpus`, and says so.

**Ask, sentence by sentence: met, with two fixes close-out makes (ledger items 1 and 2).**
- **W5:** met.
  - `live` is gone, and the three renamed rows keep their cells.
  - The four unhalted follow-up rows are there. The `running` difference names neither `queueIfBusy` nor `force`; the `stopped` difference names `guardRunStopped` and the kit's finished `stopped` rows (LIN-3675).
  - The `none` row's outcome comes from `resolveFollowUp`. Only follow-up rows get their own ledger; halt-text and `setup()` keep `running`.
  - Both drivers throw on `live` and unknown values. The census iterates the driver's own vocabulary. The kit learned no stopped refusal: `resolveFollowUp` is unchanged.
- **W1:** met. The seven rows are unchanged. The two new rows read as asked. The by-name check replaces the count. There is no `[done]` row, and the `[done]` sentence is in the top-level `note`. There is no `areas` key. No matcher file changed.
- **W8:** met.
  - Synthetic lines are skipped before keying (`runner.mjs:634`), and the first non-synthetic line sets the model (`:595`).
  - The fallback, the all-zero filter and the `keepMax` lines are untouched. `found` is removed, and the fold has one caller.
  - Both doc comments are rewritten, and lin-4202 `:126` now covers a no-id synthetic line (its `line()` helper adds no id).
  - The `fold` area has 14 rows. I recomputed all 8 corpus sha256 values and they match.
  - The render keeps `""` apart from absent, and both corners are asserted `kit !== sd`. The note says what `fold` compares and excludes.
- **W6:** met. Four witness cases, including snapshot to no usage, plus a positive control. `lib/run-paragraph.js` and `lib/run-paragraph-hook.js` are byte-identical to base (`cmp`).
- **Docs and pin:** met.
  - W1, W4, W5 and W8 are removed, and W6 is rewritten with all four parts of its answer.
  - Lessons are 6,019 bytes at both base and head by the guard's `lessonsBytes`.
  - `CONTRACT_SHA256` equals the file's sha at every commit: `7dc619762` 616edd49, `4436d443c` onward 871ca615. Only those two commits touch `contract.json`.
- **`sd` cells:** met. The SD branch `feat/lin-4476-session-fold-drivers` at `f98e442` sits on `47fb6af`, and `cmp` says its fixture is identical to the head `contract.json`. I ran SD's contract test there: 92 tests, 89 pass, 0 fail, 3 skipped (the existing unpinned rows). The session, report and all 14 fold rows pass by name, as do SD's W-2 and the phase test. The SD commit is named in the LV test header and the PR body.
- **Testing:** met. I swapped in base `runner.mjs` and inline 1–3, the `model ""` corner and lin-4202 `:126` went red. My own run of the six touched suites: 201/201.
- **Plan-review Notes 1–3:** met (top-level `note`; `""` kept distinct; doc comments and `:126`).
- **"Where the code shows it is wrong, change course and say so on LIN-4461."** The course change (an unhalted `none` row, because the plan's W-1 census can't hold without one) is built and explained on LIN-4475 and in the PR. It isn't on LIN-4461. One comment fully closes that gap and the delivered work doesn't change, so it's a fix close-out makes, not a cut (ledger item 1).

**Mutation checks** (scratch worktrees only; every revert proven with an empty `git status` and `git diff`):
- Every load-bearing rule went red for the right reason:
  - the kit map (live accepted, `stopped`/`finished` sent to absent); the census (deleting each of the unhalted `none`, `running` and `stopped` rows, with the pin fixed, fails W-1 alone); each new report cell; a missing sentinel twin;
  - every fold rule (synthetic after keying, last model wins, a later line fills the model, no `requestId` fallback, no all-zero filter, keeping `""` model or `""` timestamp); a corpus row's sha; one flipped corpus byte (fails with `bed855a5…` against `27515938…`); lin-4202 `:126`;
  - `cost`, then `tier`, added to `gateFacts` (fails the W-6 cases the PR names); the gate forced to always hit (fails the positive control);
  - SD: `finished` sent to EXECUTING and `stopped` to COMPLETED, `live` accepted, `""` rendered as null (fails both corners), one flipped corpus byte.
- One survivor: kit `finished: 'done'` → `'running'` stays green, because `resolveFollowUp` continues any row that isn't `lost`, so the kit acts the same on done and running rows. That is the kit's real behaviour (the "possibly deeper" survey point the ask declined), not a test gap.
- Test level: unit throughout is right; the cross-repo seam is covered by the byte-identical fixture and SD's own run. The contract test went from about 197 ms to about 205 ms (94 → 120 tests).

**Regression:** intact. LIN-3212's per-id maximum, LIN-3670's no-session follow-up under stop, LIN-3675's stopped rows, the LIN-4202/4203 corpus oracles, the LIN-4384 shape check and the LIN-4378 forward row are all still there. Nothing reverted.

**Class:** isolated. Other `live` values in either repo mean something else (queue source, pid verdicts). The kit's `out.live` (`runner.mjs:437`) is outside: the survey's "named ledger states" item. SD's piece-0 oracle walk `test/helpers/transcript-corpus-walk.js` still drops `<synthetic>` after keying; it's outside, excluded by the plan, and its header says it must not be changed to match. `columnProblems` is gone from SD code. No other summary gate hashes cost, usage or tier.

**Noted, not a ledger item:**
- `docs/areas/README.md` says settled Waiting entries leave, but the ask says to rewrite W6 in place, which is what was built. If the convention should win, the person who owns it can delete that bullet in a one-line follow-up.
- Fold on real transcripts: a request whose first usage line has no model (or `""`) is now unpriced. The plan and the ask chose that on purpose to match SD's `walkRequestRecords`, and the corpus rows and the eight-file oracle pin it; correctness doesn't depend on how often it happens. If it ever occurs, it shows in the cost read as fold `completeness: 'unpriced'` with `'unknown'` in `unpricedModels` (`lib/request-usage-fold.js:103-105`).
- The positional "Waiting N" comments at `tests/unit/lin-4455-kinds-and-constants-characterization.test.js:18,22` drift further. This is outside the ticket and the builder noted it.

### What CI Did Not Prove
1. **The change of course isn't recorded on LIN-4461.** Inside (the ask's "say so on LIN-4461"). Fix close-out makes before the merge: post this comment on LIN-4461: "LIN-4475 changed course from the plan's W-1: the census needs an unhalted follow-up row for every session value, so a `none` row was added to `lib/runner-kit/contract.json` (`follow-up with no live session with no halt`: sd failed, kit failed) beside the plan's finished, running and stopped rows. PR #2448." Discharged when that comment exists on LIN-4461.
2. **No `### Leftovers` comment and no `Retires:` line.** Inside (the leftover step; review checks the line names a Waiting entry the diff removes). `Retires:` names "the waiting entry the build settled" (`RETIRES_LABEL`, `lib/prompts/leftover-words.js`), and this diff removes four, so naming one of them satisfies the check without widening the ticket. Fix close-out makes before the merge: post on LIN-4475 a comment whose body is
   `### Leftovers`
   `Retires: \`lib/runner-kit/runner.mjs\`: the per-message transcript fold is here and in SD`
   That is the W8 entry's cited file and opening words, as they stand at `origin/main`. Discharged when the comment exists and that line matches an entry the diff removes.
3. **Stale `sd` cells re-verify.** Inside. Satisfied right now (verified: SD `origin/main` is `47fb6af`, and `contract.json` hasn't changed since `4436d443c`). Route, before the merge: if the PR head is no longer `68b3e5f4` with `contract.json` sha `871ca615…`, or SD `origin/main` is no longer `47fb6af`, re-copy the contract into `feat/lin-4476-session-fold-drivers`, rebase it on SD `origin/main`, and re-run `node --require ./test/isolate-run.js --require ./test/state-cache-trap.js --test test/runner-contract.test.js` (0 fail required) before merging. If neither moved, it's discharged at merge time.
4. **CI on the merge commit to main.** Inside (the ask: "LV's full suite and CI are green on the merge commit"). Route, after the merge: the `test.yml` run on the main merge commit passes every check. Rollback: this repo squash-merges (single-parent PR commits on `--first-parent`; it occasionally uses merge commits), so the rollback is one `git revert` of #2448's squash commit, or `git revert -m 1` of its merge commit. It's genuinely reversible: test, fixture and kit-fold code only, with nothing stored in a new shape. Records already posted keep their fields, and the kit returns to last-model pricing after a revert.
5. **PR 3: re-copy and both pins equal.** Outside this PR; its home is the existing ticket LIN-4476 (blocked by LIN-4475; nothing to file). After the merge, LIN-4476 copies `contract.json` from #2448's merge commit and re-pins `LV_COMMIT` and `FIXTURE_SHA256`. LIN-4461 close-out then checks with `cmp` that the two files are identical at both `origin/main`s.

### Verdict
Approve — conditional on close-out discharging the ledger

## Autopilot stepper run summary: review step (LIN-4475)

Engine pick: `review` (PR #2448 open, CI green, no review yet). Stepped as 4 beats in one fresh warm session (ROOT `59599417-43ac-497c-8bf3-51d498a22a3e`) with no memory of the build; the reviewer was told to treat every comment, including mine, as a claim to verify.

- **Beat 1/4** ground, scope, CI (3m 2s): head `68b3e5f4`, six files all named by the ask or plan, CI confirmed per check on that exact SHA, SD fixture hash matched.
- **Beat 2/4** (`78a833fb`, 7m) the ask sentence by sentence, the don't-clauses by command, SD's contract test re-run from the pushed branch (89 pass, 0 fail), regression and gap checks.
- **Beat 3/4** (`2dc6e2c5`, 11m 48s) test quality and mutation checks: about thirty mutations across LV and SD, each red for the right reason, every revert proven clean; the one survivor (kit `finished` mapped to `running`) is a real absence of a kit distinction, not a test gap.
- **Beat 4/4** (`1155aec5`, 14m 52s) ledger and verdict.

**Verified by me:** the review comment `cfcc5ab7-fa42-425d-af96-25e0c25f5481` exists on this ticket and names head `68b3e5f428740954ffa38d264bcddceb07d6f035`, which is still PR #2448's head (open, clean, mergeable); LV `main` is still `ca77a891e`, SD `main` still `47fb6af`, the SD branch still `f98e442`; the `Retires:` text it proposes matches the W8 entry on `main` word for word.

**Two calls I put to the reviewer before it wrote the verdict, and what it concluded:** (1) the missing note on LIN-4461 is a fix close-out makes, not a cut, because one comment fully closes it and the delivered work does not change; (2) the `Retires:` rule is satisfied by naming an entry the diff already removes, so nothing is added to a ticket sized "just the task". It also marked the PR 3 re-copy as outside this ticket (home: LIN-4476, already open) and kept the fold-on-real-transcripts risk out of the ledger as a deliberate, plan-chosen behaviour, naming the real signal if it ever occurs.

**Verdict:** Approve, conditional on close-out discharging the ledger: post the LIN-4461 course-change comment, post the `### Leftovers` comment with its `Retires:` line, re-verify the stale-cell rule at merge time, then merge and confirm CI on the merge commit. Rollback named: one revert of the PR's squash commit.

**What is left:** `close-out`. Not merged, not Done.

## Blind read
Verdict: better. It made things better in three places. In `lib/runner-kit/runner.mjs` the fold lost its dead `found` flag, and its synthetic/model rule moved into one keying step, now pinned by contract rows that fail against the base code. `tests/unit/runner-kit-contract.test.js` now judges follow-ups with the real `resolveFollowUp` against a ledger for each session value, not a hand-coded `session === 'none'` shortcut, and it checks the report rows by name, not by count. Against that, it made things worse in one way: the expected records for the eight transcript-corpus files now live twice, in `lib/runner-kit/contract.json` and in `tests/fixtures/cost-replay/corpus.js`, and the contract's `note` keeps growing as prose.

Read: https://github.com/JKershaw/LinearViewer/pull/2448 at `68b3e5f42` against `ca77a891e`.

### Inside the area, fix-sized
- `tests/unit/runner-kit-contract.test.js` (runs-and-dispatch): the `fold` corpus rows hard-code the same per-request records that `LIN4197_CASES[...].records` in `tests/fixtures/cost-replay/corpus.js` already pins, and `tests/unit/lin-4202-runner-kit-records.test.js` checks them. A change to the fold rule now means editing two copies, and nothing ties them together. Fix: in the contract test, assert that each corpus row's `sd` equals `renderFold(LIN4197_CASES[row.item.id].records)`. Then the two copies cannot drift apart without a failure.
- `tests/unit/runner-kit-contract.test.js` (runs-and-dispatch): the new file-header comment names an unmerged SD commit and branch that it calls "superseded", plus a future "PR 3 (LIN-4476)" that will re-pin. That comment goes stale the moment the follow-up lands. Fix: drop it, or cut it down to a pointer at the SD-side `LV_COMMIT`/`FIXTURE_SHA256` pin.
- `tests/unit/runner-kit-contract.test.js` (runs-and-dispatch): the session vocabulary is spelled out three times: in `SESSION_LEDGER_STATE`, in the hand-written list inside `sessionLedger`'s error message, and in `contract.json`'s `note`. Fix: build the error text from `Object.keys(SESSION_LEDGER_STATE)`.
- `lib/runner-kit/runner.mjs` (runs-and-dispatch): `transcriptRequestRecords` now counts `skipped.synthetic` per line, where it used to count per request, while `skipped.zero` still counts per request. A streamed `<synthetic>` message spread over three lines reports `synthetic: 3` in the `usage` command's `records.skipped`. Fix: state the unit of each counter in the docblock, or count distinct synthetic keys.

### Inside the area, larger
- `lib/run-ledger.js` (runs-and-dispatch): the new report row records that Harbour's `PR_URL_RE` reads https only, while SD canonicalises an `http://` DONE: URL to https. The row pins the divergence as a `difference` instead of resolving it. This is larger than a fix because deciding which reader is right, and whether Harbour's PR reading should widen, is a design call that affects every run's PR attribution.

### Outside the area
- `lib/runner-kit/contract.json` (unmapped: the fix is in the simple-dispatcher repo): the two fold corners (a first line with model `""` or timestamp `""`) are left as declared differences. SD posts an empty `at`, which Harbour's intake rejects, so the fix belongs in SD's `walkRequestRecords`, not here.

## Autopilot note before close-out: blind-read finds against the ask (LIN-4475)

The blind read (`6fb3fa58`, verdict better) was done without the ask, by design. Two things worth having in front of whoever acts on its finds:

1. **Its second fix-sized find would cut an ask clause.** It says to drop the new header comment in `tests/unit/runner-kit-contract.test.js` that names the SD verification commit. The ask says, in the `## As asked` block, "Name the verified SD commit in the contract test's header and in the PR description." The clause has to stay delivered: shortening the comment to just the SD commit and its branch, and what it is for, keeps it; deleting it does not.
2. **Any change to `lib/runner-kit/contract.json` reopens the stale-cell rule** (review ledger item 3, the ask's "re-copy, rebase and re-run SD's contract test before this PR merges"). The other fix-sized finds are in test code and doc comments, so they do not need to touch that file. The review approved head `68b3e5f428740954ffa38d264bcddceb07d6f035`; a fix commit on top is a new head, so CI has to be green on the exact commit that merges.

Also already tracked, for whoever sorts the outside-the-area find: SD's `""` timestamp corner is the leftover the plan assigns to PR 3 (LIN-4476), named in this PR's description and in the review. Both facts are recorded; neither changes what the blind read found.

### Leftovers
Retires: `lib/runner-kit/runner.mjs`: the per-message transcript fold is here and in SD

## Close-out — LIN-4475

**Merged.** https://github.com/JKershaw/LinearViewer/pull/2448, squash-merged as `302edafc3a27a8d0d64a88435766625ab8d24cb5` on `main`, pinned with `--match-head-commit 6901d1eb579cf5cd20893fdfeba4c213e91d241c` (the commit CI passed on).

**Against what was asked.** Review's account (`cfcc5ab7-fa42-425d-af96-25e0c25f5481`) of W5, W1, W8, W6, docs and pin, `sd` cells and testing stands: close-out changed no behaviour, only what review and the blind read named. Nothing in the `## As asked` block was cut. The plan was implemented as approved, with these deviations: an unhalted `none` follow-up row so the census holds, the dead `found` flag removed from the fold, the corpus under `tests/fixtures/runner-kit/transcript-corpus`, and `caseKeyOf` not reused.

| Commit | Change | Answers |

So no re-copy, rebase or SD re-run was needed (SD branch `f98e442` was verified at `871ca615` against `47fb6af`).
4. **CI on the merge commit + rollback:** settled. Run https://github.com/JKershaw/LinearViewer/actions/runs/43536956025 on `302edafc3`: Unit tests, Unit tests (proxy, clock +400d), E2E shards 1/4–4/4, Secret scan (source) and CI success all concluded success, each `head_sha` `302edafc3`. Note: an earlier `related` link I added between the two replaced the original `blocks` relation; I restored `blocks` (new relation id `eda48420…`), so the pair carries `blocks` only.

**Deploy.** `main` deploys (Harbour's page footer shows its deployed commit). It read `ca77a891e` before the merge and `302edafc3a27a8d0d64a88435766625ab8d24cb5` at 00:58:57Z, seen by reading the footer's commit link on https://harbour.cat/. Review's ledger names no post-deploy step, and none was run.

### Blind read's finds, and where each went
- Four fix-sized finds: fixed (`d17175aff`, `2ab402643`, `573566250`, `c0e589fd8`).
- http/https PR-link divergence: one `## Waiting` entry in `docs/areas/runs-and-dispatch.md` (no ticket).

### Local and CI state
Bearing tests on the final head: contract, lin-4202, lin-4375, area-notes, run-paragraph-hook 186/186; the area guards and contract test 150/150. PR head `6901d1eb5`: all 8 checks green, run https://github.com/JKershaw/LinearViewer/actions/runs/43536092301.

## Autopilot stepper run summary: close-out and the whole run (LIN-4475)

description:
## As asked

**Parent:** LIN-4461 (Runs & dispatch: cross-repository contract with simple-dispatcher, piece 8 of LIN-4447). **Repository:** JKershaw/LinearViewer (LV), plus a prepared, unmerged branch in JKershaw/simple-dispatcher (SD) used to fill the `sd` cells. **Landing order:** PR 2 of 3. It is blocked by the PR 1 subtask (SD `columnProblems` retired).

**Starting point:** LIN-4461's approved plan. Read the `## Implementation Plan` section of LIN-4461's description in full: W1, W5, W6 and W8 under "Which way", "PR 2" under "Per repository, per PR", "How stale `sd` cells are caught", and witnesses W-1, W-2, W-3, W-5 and W-6. Read the approving verdict (comment f912859d) too, especially its three **Notes for the builder**. Follow that plan. Where the code shows it is wrong, change course and say so on LIN-4461.

## This piece's slice of the approved plan

**Session contract (W5, the ticket's Waiting 7):** in `lib/runner-kit/contract.json`, replace `live` with `running | finished | stopped | none`.

* LV's kit driver maps these to the kit ledger values `running | done | stopped | absent`.
* SD's driver (on the PR 3 branch) maps them to `EXECUTING | COMPLETED | CANCELLED | absent`.
* Rename the three existing `live` rows to `finished`, keeping their outcome cells.
* Add unhalted follow-up rows:
  * `finished`: both sides claim.
  * `running`: SD failed, kit claimed. The `difference` says the row covers neither `queueIfBusy` nor `force`.
  * `stopped`: SD failed, kit claimed. The `difference` says Harbour's admission gate owns the refusal, and kit `stopped` rows can be finished subagents.
* The `none` row's `failed` outcome comes from `resolveFollowUp`, not a hard-coded line.
* In `tests/unit/runner-kit-contract.test.js`, build a ledger from the row's session value **for follow-up rows only**. The `halt-text` rows and the take-driven `setup()` tests keep today's `running` ledger.
* The driver throws on `live` and on any unknown value. Update the take-driven unknown-repository fixture too.
* Add a census: every session value in use has an unhalted follow-up row.
* Don't teach the kit a stopped-session refusal.

**Reported PRs (W1, the ticket's Waiting 1,** `sessionPrs`**):** SD owns the rule.

* Keep the seven LIN-4384 report rows. Add two:
  * `DONE: http://github.com/<o>/<r>/pull/<n>#x`: SD returns canonical https, Harbour returns null, with a `difference`.
  * `DONE:` after U+2028: both return the PR.
* Replace the exact-seven census with a check that the seven named cases remain, each with `harbour === sd` and a sentinel twin.
* No `[done]` row. Its reading stays pinned by `tests/unit/lin-4375-session-pr-wins.test.js:54`. Put the `[done]` boundary sentence in the contract's **top-level** `note`. There is no per-area note slot, and you must not add an `areas` table.
* Don't move or merge the PR matchers.

**Transcript fold (W8, the ticket's Waiting 13):** SD's `walkRequestRecords` owns the rule.

* In `lib/runner-kit/runner.mjs`, change the kit fold (`foldTranscriptMessages`/`transcriptRequestRecords`) in two ways:
  1. Skip `<synthetic>` lines before keying.
  2. Take the model from the first non-synthetic line, even when that line has none.
* Keep the request-ID fallback, the all-zero filtering and the per-field maxima unchanged.
* Rewrite both functions' doc comments, and update the `tests/unit/lin-4202-runner-kit-records.test.js` `:126` expectation and comment: synthetic usage lines are counted before keying, including a synthetic line with no ID.
* Add contract area `fold` (inputs none, columns `kit`) to `AREA_SHAPES`:
  * 8 shared corpus rows, with ids `<case>/<phase>` plus each file's SHA-256. LV maps the ids to its own paths and checks the bytes before folding.
  * 4 agreeing inline cases:
    1. a real line then a synthetic line under one ID;
    2. two models under one ID;
    3. a first line with no model, then a line with one;
    4. the `requestId` fallback beside an all-zero request.
  * 2 declared-difference cases: first line `model: ""` and first line `timestamp: ""`.
* Render records deterministically in first-seen order, comparing `requestId`, `model`, `at` and the five token fields. Render absent as `null` and keep `""` as `""`. Add both corner rows to the deliberate-differences census, asserting `kit !== sd`.
* The top-level `note` says what `fold` compares and what it excludes (`harness`, `agent`, `effort`, skipped counts, and SD attribution across transcripts).

**Stored paragraphs (W6, the ticket's Waiting 10):** add a witness to `tests/unit/run-paragraph-hook.test.js` (beside `lib/run-paragraph-hook.js`) and leave production code unchanged.

* A stored `final` paragraph stays a cache hit, with no generator call, when only cost, usage or tier change. That includes a lineage that falls from snapshot figures to `no-usage`.
* A newly ended loop still regenerates it.
* Show in the PR description that the witness fails when a cost field is temporarily added to the hash input.
* **Accepted cut, quoted:** "label them pre-cutover" is not delivered. John accepted the cut in LIN-4461 comment e1e70bac: stored paragraphs never carried a figure, so a label would point at nothing.

**Docs and pin:**

* In `docs/areas/runs-and-dispatch.md`, remove W1, W4, W5 and W8. Rewrite W6 with the answer: stored text is retained, the cutover doesn't regenerate it, it contains no figure to label, and the witness test is named.
* Add no LV Lesson. Lessons stay under 6,144 bytes; measure them now.
* Update `CONTRACT_SHA256` in the same commit as `contract.json`.

**Filling the** `sd` **cells:**

* Prepare the PR 3 branch in SD: SD's driver changes plus a copy of this PR's head `contract.json`, rebased on SD `origin/main`. Run SD's drivers from it to fill and verify the `sd` cells.
* Name the verified SD commit in the contract test's header and in the PR description.
* If this PR changes after review, or SD `origin/main` moves, re-copy, rebase and re-run SD's contract test **before this PR merges**.

**Testing:**

* Witnesses W-1, W-2, W-3, W-5 (inline cases 1–3 fail before the change and pass after; a one-byte corpus tamper in a temp copy fails its sha check) and W-6.
* `lin-4202-runner-kit-records` stays green.
* LV's full suite and CI are green on the merge commit.
* SD's contract test passes on the prepared branch.

**Retires:** LV's halves of W1, W5 and W8 as unpinned copies, the double meaning of `live`, and the W4 and W8 Waiting entries. W6 is settled in place. Say what it retires in the PR.

**Acceptance:** the PR is merged with the above in place, `CONTRACT_SHA256` matches the merged `contract.json`, the `sd` cells are verified against a named SD commit, and the prepared PR 3 branch exists for the next subtask.

Session fit: fits one session
Plan-review due: no — covered by LIN-4461's approving plan-review (comment f912859d-0598-4959-9f54-1d0f491aded4, rev 2)
Grounding commits: LinearViewer `e666c4b60` and SD `1616b19c3`, both still `origin/main` at breakdown (13 Nov, 20:30Z). Re-check both heads before building.

*End of what was asked. Steps write below this line; nothing above it changes.*

## Size of the move

**Size:** just the task
**Why:** Delivers this repo's slice of the parent's consolidation as asked, giving each session value one meaning, the reported-PR and transcript-fold rules one owner each, and stored paragraphs a witness; no finding opens a larger move.
**Cuts:** none
**Decided by:** the standing policy

## Implemented

Merged: [https://github.com/JKershaw/LinearViewer/pull/2448](<https://github.com/JKershaw/LinearViewer/pull/2448>) (squash commit 302edafc3a27a8d0d64a88435766625ab8d24cb5), CI green on the PR head and on the merge commit, deployed.

The approved plan from LIN-4461 was implemented as approved: the session vocabulary (running | finished | stopped | none), the two report rows, the kit fold with its contract area, and the stored-paragraph witness. Deviations: an unhalted `none` follow-up row was added so the census holds; the dead `found` flag was removed from the fold; the corpus files are under `tests/fixtures/runner-kit/transcript-corpus`; `caseKeyOf` was not reused.

What is left belongs to LIN-4476 (the SD copy of the merged contract and its pins). The full history of this ticket is preserved in its task snapshots and the comment trail, including the review, the blind read and the close-out summary.
